title.narrative: Världsbanken - Sudan Transition and Recovery Support Trust Fund (STARS)
World Bank - Sudan Transition and Recovery Support Trust Fund (STARS)

description.narrative: Sida became a contributor to the World Bank managed Sudan Transition and Recovery Support Trust Fund (STARS) in 2020. The Sudan Family Support Program (SFSP) 2020-2022 was the first major project funded by STARS. The objective of the intervention was to deliver cash transfer support to Sudanese households affected by expected economic reforms and other short-term shocks. The project was implemented together with the government. After the military coup and the subsequent civil war, the World Bank remained engaged in line with its Strategy for Fragility, Conflict, and Violence and adjustments were made to STARS in order to respond to the new challenges in an operational environment that had changed significantly. STARS consequently turned to third party implementation and currently the Thabat project is the main project of the trust fund. The Thabat project is supporting community resilience and aims to preserve human capital, improve access to basic services and food security, protect institutional capacity, and support early preparation for a post-conflict recovery. The project is implemented by United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), the World Food Programme (WFP), Mercy Corps and the Catholic Relief Services (CRS) focusing on two main components: Component 1: Community-led Basic Service Delivery. This component supports (i) the delivery of improved community-led basic services, including health and nutrition, alternative education programs, WASH services, and services against gender-based violence (GBV); (ii) temporary engagement of frontline workers (FLWs) and volunteers in selected sectors; (iii) project management and technical assistance (TA); and (iv) TA and training for selected local authorities. Component 2: Improving Food Security. This component supports (i) increased resilience and production of select crops and protection of livestock assets in rural areas that supply food to the target communities, (ii) agricultural value chains, (iii) the scaling-up and strengthening of community consumer cooperatives and organizations and community food centers that distribute agricultural outputs and provide affordable food to vulnerable groups, and (iv) project management and implementation costs.

Sida blev bidragsgivare till den Världsbanksförvaltade Sudan Transition and Recovery Support Trust Fund (STARS) år 2020. Sudan Family Support Program (SFSP) 2020-2022 var det första större projektet som finansierades av STARS. Projektets syfte var att tillhandahålla kontantstöd till sudanesiska hushåll som skulle drabbades av förväntade ekonomiska reformer och andra kortsiktiga chocker. Projektet genomfördes tillsammans med regeringen. Efter militärkuppen och det efterföljande inbördeskriget fortsatte Världsbanken att engagera sig i Sudans utveckling i linje med sin Strategy for Fragility, Conflict, and Violence. Justeringar gjordes i STARS för att bemöta de nya utmaningarna i en operativ miljö som hade förändrats avsevärt. STARS övergick följaktligen till tredjepartsimplementering och för närvarande är Thabat-projektet fondens huvudprojekt. Thabat-projektet stöder samhällens motståndskraft och syftar till att bevara humankapital, förbättra tillgången till grundläggande samhällstjänster och livsmedelssäkerhet, skydda institutionell kapacitet och stödja tidiga förberedelser för en återhämtning efter konfliket. Projektet genomförs av FN:s barnfond (UNICEF), Världslivsmedelsprogrammet (WFP), Mercy Corps och Catholic Relief Services (CRS) med fokus på två huvudkomponenter: Komponent 1: lokalsamhällens tillhandahållande av grundläggande samhälltjänstelever . Denna komponent stöder (i) leverans av grundläggande samhällstjänster, inklusive hälsa och näring, alternativa utbildningsprogram, vatten-, sanerings- och hygientjänster och tjänster mot könsbaserat våld; (ii) tillfälligt engagemang av tidigare personal så som lärare och vårdpersonal och av volontärer inom utvalda sektorer; (iii) projektledning och tekniskt bistånd; och (iv) tekniskt bistånd och utbildning för utvalda lokala myndigheter.
Komponent 2: Förbättrad livsmedelssäkerhet. Denna komponent stöder (i) ökad motståndskraft och produktion av utvalda grödor samt skydd av boskapsstocken på landsbygden som levererar mat till målgrupperna, (ii) jordbruksvärdekedjor, (iii) uppskalning och förstärkning av lokala konsumentkooperativ och organisationer samt lokala livsmedelscentraler som distribuerar jordbruksprodukter och tillhandahåller prisvärd mat till utsatta grupper, och (iv) projektlednings- och implementeringsstöd.

The Sudan Transition and Recovery Support Trust Fund (STARS) Multi-Donor Trust Fund was established in April 2020 after the restructuring of the Sudan Multi-Partner Fund (SMPF). STARS is an umbrella coordination platform for World Bank engagement in Sudan. The objective of STARS is to support the Government of Sudans economic and peacebuilding transition and building systems, including for crisis response.
The military coup in 2021 and then the subsequent outbreak of civil war between rival faction of the military government in April 2023 have resulted in adjustment of the STARS' engagement. The Sudanese de facto government is no longer part of the Partnership Council governance of the trust fund and is not an implementing party STARs funded projects.
The two main STARS funded programs of engagement since the coup in 2021 are:
- Sudan Emergency Safety Nets Project (SESNP) with the objective to provide cash transfers and food support to food insecure households in selected Project Areas of Sudan and implemented by WFP (July 2022 September 2023) and,
- Sudan Thabat Project - Enhancing Community Resilience Project with the objective to support to resilient development of conflict affected communities in Sudan implemented by WFP, UNICEF, Mercy Corps and Catholic Relief Services (April 2024 August 2026).

This update is a slightly edited version of the summery provided in the WB annual report for the Sudan Transition and Recovery Support multi-donor trust fund (STARS TF) for the period July 2024 to June 2025.
The implementation of the main STARS financed project, the Sudan Thabat Project supporting resilient development of conflict affected communities in Sudan, was accelerated during the reporting period 2024/2025 and the main results include:
The project restored essential services to communities, including establishing 24 community development committees (CDCs); rehabilitating water facilities that serve 187,000 beneficiaries; providing essential health, nutrition, and population services to 138,720 beneficiaries; and setting up 60 accelerated learning programs (ALPs) with over 9,000 children enrolled (53 percent female) and more than 1,700 frontline workers (FLWs) mobilized across sectors. on food security and the agricultural value chain, the Sudan Thabat Project supported 25,000 farmer households to harvest 73,000 MT of wheat, equivalent to 18 percent of the national wheat production in the 2024/25 winter season.
Building on the successful implementation, two Additional Financing projects were formulated in FY25 (US$60 million from the STARS TF and US$50 million from the International Development Association, IDA).
Advisory Services and Analytics (ASAs) supported by STARS TF, and mostly performed by WB staff and consultants, set the basis for evidence-based programs and reconstruction in the future. The key products are the Sudan Economic Update and four rounds of the Sudan Welfare System Monitoring Survey. In addition, to prepare for reconstruction in the future, the STARS TF partners agreed to finance eight new ASAs, including the Economic and Social Impact Assessment of the Conflict.
The main lessons learned during the during implementation 2024/2025 include:
Selecting the right implementation partner. Under the challenging operational environment, most STARS TF partners and the World Bank had limited field presence. Thus, selecting the right implementation partner based on areas of expertise and geographical targeting is critical. The selection criteria should include the partners engagement with local NGOs, institutions, and contractors for partnership and sustainability.
- Keeping focus on development work with the nexus of humanitarian assistance. For example, building local institutional capacity contributes to emergency response with long-term sustainability. Likewise, engaging with the private sector is expected to have lasting impacts. During the implementation of the Sudan Thabat Project, its development impacts will have to be closely monitored. Feedback from BSMA and analytical works (for example, Sudan Welfare System Monitoring Survey) are expected to supplement the project-level M&E.
- Broadening collaboration and partnership. STARS TF has been instrumental as a coordination platform among the STARS TF partners and the World Bank. In FY25, STARS TF convened meetings with other development actors and demonstrated its potential to broaden engagement with various development actors. Given the rapid change in the aid landscape and proliferation of development actors, it is important to continue the efforts, including in the areas of data and information collection.
Challenges
The ongoing conflict has had severe economic, social, and humanitarian impacts, leading to a shrinking economy and soaring inflation. The conflict has caused significant loss of life and property, extensive infrastructure damage, major disruptions to essential services and economic activities, displacement, and escalating humanitarian needs. As a result, the estimated poverty rate stands at 71 percent, and the unemployment rate is estimated at 47 percent. The ongoing conflict between the Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has made development assistance challenging. Additionally, the lack of field presence by STARS TF partners and the World Bank has been a constraint for implementing the activities supported by STARS TF. Globally, changes in the aid landscape have had adverse impacts on aid flows to Sudan.
